newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF files complaint with prosecutors vs DKB - source.
newsitem.headline: MOF files complaint with prosecutors vs DKB - source.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry filed a complaint with Tokyo prosecutors on Friday against Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) and some former DKB executives for alleged violations of the Banking Law, a financial source said.
The alleged violations involved concealing information about a scandal involving payoffs to a corporate racketeer, the source said.
The financial source did not elaborate further on the complaint filed with prosecutors.
No bank has ever been fined for such a violation, which carries a maximum penalty of a 500,000 yen fine.
More than a dozen people, including top executives from DKB and Nomura Securities Co Ltd, have been arrested in the racketeer scandal.
Administrative punishment against Nomura is expected to be announced next week and Kyodo news agency said on Friday that penalties against DKB could also be announced next week.
Japanese media said prosecutors were set to indict later on Friday former DKB chairman Tadashi Okuda for illegal bank loans to the "sokaiya" racketeer at the heart of the affair.
